items.summary_en: Police 112, fire and ambulance 119. Both are free and open 24 hours, and both can connect an interpreter.

steps.title_en: Police: call 112
steps.body_en: Free, 24 hours. Police can add an English or Chinese interpreter to your call (3-way call).
steps.show_staff_en: Please connect me with an English interpreter.

steps.title_en: Fire, rescue or ambulance: call 119
steps.body_en: Free, 24 hours. The ambulance is free. 119 gives hospital information, first-aid help and interpretation in English, Chinese, Japanese, Mongolian and Vietnamese. If you can't talk, you can report by text, photo or video through the 119 app or website.

steps.title_en: Not an emergency? Call 1330
steps.body_en: Lost, need a quick interpreter, or have a travel question: call the Korea Travel Helpline 1330 (from a foreign phone: +82-2-1330).

steps.title_en: Get disaster alerts in your language
steps.body_en: Install the government's 'Emergency Ready' app for safety alerts in English, Chinese, Vietnamese, Thai and Japanese.

sources.field: 112 interpretation: English and Chinese, 3-way, 24 hours (announced March 2024)
119 languages: EN, ZH, JA, MN, VI

items.summary_en: Your new passport or emergency travel document comes from your own country's embassy, not from Korea. Most embassies ask for a Korean police report first, so start at a police station.

steps.title_en: Look again and call the last places you visited
steps.body_en: Hotel, restaurant, taxi company. The Korea Travel Helpline 1330 can interpret for you.

steps.title_en: Report it at a police station
steps.body_en: Any police station (경찰서) or police box (파출소 / 지구대) takes lost-item reports. Ask for a written confirmation of your report — your embassy will likely ask for it. You can also report online, but it needs a Korean login.
steps.show_staff_ko: 여권을 잃어버렸습니다. 분실 신고를 하고 확인서를 받고 싶습니다.
steps.show_staff_en: I lost my passport. I'd like to report it and get a confirmation.

steps.title_en: Contact your embassy
steps.body_en: Each country has its own rules. Some need the police report, some don't. Most can give you an emergency travel document within a working day or two — but it may only let you fly home, not to another country. Call before you go.

steps.title_en: Living in Korea? Tell immigration about your new passport
steps.body_en: If you have a Residence Card, report the new passport within 15 days. It's free — online on HiKorea, or at your immigration office with a booking. Bring the form, your new passport and your Residence Card. Late reports can be fined.

items.summary_en: Lost it in a taxi and paid by card? Call the number on your receipt right away — it's the fastest way to find the car. Anything else: report it at a police station or search Police Civil Service 24.

steps.title_en: Lost it in a taxi
steps.body_en: If you paid by card, the driver's or company's phone number is on the receipt — call it now. If you paid with a T-money card, T-money's lost-item service can find the taxi (online 24 hours, or call 1644-1188, weekdays 09:00–18:00, lunch 13:00–14:00). Paid cash with no receipt? Report it at a police station.
steps.show_staff_en: I left something in the taxi.

steps.title_en: Lost it on the Seoul subway (Lines 1–8)
steps.body_en: Seoul Metro has 4 Lost & Found Centers: City Hall (Lines 1–2, 02-6110-1122), Chungmuro (Lines 3–4, 02-6110-3344), Wangsimni (Lines 5 and 8, 02-6311-6765) and Taereung (Lines 6–7, 02-6311-6766). Weekdays 09:00–18:00 only. Items stay there 7 days, then go to the police.

steps.title_en: Anywhere else: police
steps.body_en: Walk into any police station or police box (파출소) and report it. You can also search found items on Police Civil Service 24 — the English version is machine-translated, and reporting online needs a Korean login.
steps.show_staff_en: I would like to report a lost item.

steps.title_en: After you report
steps.body_en: Say yes to alerts when you report — you get a text or email if a matching item is found. Report as early as you can.

sources.field: Seoul Metro centers, phones, hours, 7 days

items.summary_en: For minor problems go to a pharmacy or a clinic; for anything serious or urgent, call 119 (it's free and gives foreign-language help too).

steps.title_en: Pick the right place for how bad it is
steps.body_en: For small things (cold, headache, upset stomach) go to a pharmacy (약국) — pharmacists can sell many over-the-counter medicines without a doctor's visit. For something that needs a doctor but isn't life-threatening, go to a clinic (의원) or a hospital's outpatient department. For serious or life-threatening problems, go to an emergency room (응급실) or call 119.
steps.show_staff_en: I don't feel well. Please help me.

links.label_en: Seoul Global Center — Medical Facilities for foreigners

steps.title_en: Find a hospital that speaks your language
steps.body_en: Medical Korea (run by the government's KHIDI) runs Information Centers at Seoul Station (09:00–18:00, Korean/English/Chinese/Japanese) and at Incheon Airport Terminal 1 (09:00–21:00, adds Russian), and a hotline at +82-2-1577-7129 (09:00–18:00). In Seoul, the Seoul Global Center's 24-hour Medical Referral Service can recommend an English-speaking hospital by email at medicalreferral@seoul.go.kr.

steps.title_en: Need an interpreter right now at a pharmacy or hospital
steps.body_en: Call 1330, the Korea Travel Hotline (24 hours, or +82-2-1330 from outside Korea). Tell them you need help at a pharmacy or hospital and ask them to speak with the staff or doctor for you.
steps.show_staff_en: I'm calling 1330 to ask for an interpreter, please.

steps.title_en: Emergency: call 119
steps.body_en: For accidents, severe pain, or anything urgent, call 119. Ambulances are free. 119 itself gives interpretation and hospital information in English, Chinese, Japanese, Mongolian, and Vietnamese — you don't need to dial 1339, since that number was merged into 119 back in 2012.

steps.title_en: Night, weekend, or holiday — finding an open pharmacy or clinic
steps.body_en: The National Emergency Medical Center's site e-gen.or.kr lets you search by region and date for emergency rooms, clinics, and pharmacies still open at night or on holidays. The main search tool is in Korean, so use your phone's browser translation, and call ahead to confirm hours before you go.

items.title_en: Overcharged by a taxi or shop
items.summary_en: Keep the receipt and a photo of the taxi's plate number and fare, then report it the same day — 1330 anywhere in Korea, or 120 in Seoul. Both take reports in foreign languages.

steps.title_en: Before you pay or leave
steps.body_en: Note the taxi's plate number. Ask for a printed receipt — it shows the fare, time and the taxi company's number. In a shop, keep the receipt or card record.

steps.title_en: Seoul taxi: report it on the spot
steps.body_en: Seoul taxis have a QR code: scan it to report in English, Chinese or Japanese (plate number, time, place, meter used or not, fare). Or call the Seoul Dasan Call Center 120 (foreign languages, 24 hours).
steps.show_staff_ko: 요금이 너무 비싸요. 미터기를 사용하지 않았어요.
steps.show_staff_en: This fare is too high. You didn't use the meter.

steps.title_en: Anywhere in Korea: tourist complaint
steps.body_en: Call 1330 or use the Korea Tourist Complaint Center website. They pass your case to the right office and answer in your language: Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, Russian, Vietnamese, Thai or Indonesian.

steps.title_en: Keep these as evidence
steps.body_en: Receipt, photo of the plate number and the meter, time and place, and the driver's or shop's name if you can.

items.summary_en: Shop at stores with a Tax Free sign and spend at least ₩15,000 per receipt; get your refund immediately at the store, at a downtown booth, or at the airport — but you must get the customs check done at the airport BEFORE you check in your luggage, within 3 months of buying the goods.

steps.title_en: Shop at a Tax Free store
steps.body_en: Look for a Tax Free / Tax Refund sign at the store. Your purchase on one receipt must be at least ₩15,000. Show your passport at checkout so the store can issue your tax-refund paperwork.
steps.show_staff_ko: 세금 환급(택스 리펀) 받을 수 있나요? 여권 보여드릴게요.
steps.show_staff_en: Can I get a tax refund on this? Here is my passport.

steps.title_en: Immediate refund at the store, if offered
steps.body_en: Some Tax Free stores can subtract the VAT right at checkout. For this, one receipt must be ₩15,000 or more but less than ₩1,000,000, and your total tax-free shopping for the whole trip must not go over ₩5,000,000.

steps.title_en: Refund at a downtown refund booth
steps.body_en: If you didn't get an immediate refund at the store, you can visit a downtown tax-refund booth before you leave the country. One receipt at these booths must not be over ₩6,000,000.

steps.title_en: At the airport — do this BEFORE check-in
steps.body_en: At Incheon Airport, find the tax-refund kiosk in the check-in hall before you check your bags (Terminal 1: near Gate 28; Terminal 2: near Gate 253, opposite Gate 250). Scan your passport and receipts. If the kiosk says customs inspection is needed, bring the unopened, unused goods to the customs desk before you drop off your luggage.

steps.title_en: Know the time limit
steps.body_en: You must leave Korea with the goods within 3 months of the day you bought them.

sources.field: minimum ₩15,000; airport kiosk before check-in; kiosk locations
